result.target_topic: EC Competition Matter: Rebate Fine Annulment
result.target_summary: In January 2022, the General Court annulled the EC's 2009 findings regarding rebates and the associated €1.1 billion fine, which was returned to Intel in February 2022. Although the EC appealed this finding, the Court of Justice dismissed the EC's appeal in October 2024, upholding the annulment.

previous_disclosures.section: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements > Note 19: Commitments and Contingencies > Legal Proceedings > European Commission Competition Matter
previous_disclosures.summary: In 2009, the EC found that Intel used unfair business practices, including conditional rebates and payments to prevent rival sales, in violation of Article 82 of the EC Treaty. The EC ordered Intel to end the infringement and imposed a €1.1 billion fine, which was paid in the third quarter of 2009.

current_disclosures.section: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements > Note 19: Commitments and Contingencies > Legal Proceedings > European Commission Competition Matter
current_disclosures.summary: In 2009, the European Commission found Intel violated competition law regarding rebates and payments, imposing a €1.1 billion fine which Intel paid; however, in January 2022, the General Court annulled the rebate findings and the fine, which was returned to Intel, though the finding regarding payments to prevent rival sales remained. The EC appealed the rebate annulment, but in October 2024 the Court of Justice dismissed the appeal, upholding the General Court's judgment.

Both companies are navigating high-stakes appellate proceedings, but Intel's case reached a final conclusion (dismissal of appeal) while NVIDIA's remains pending further appellate review.
